title: How to Make Instagram Reels That Sell Products in Pakistan
summary: How to make Instagram Reels that sell products in Pakistan: the 3-second hook, the five shots to film on a phone, captions, and turning views into orders.
body_markdown:
A Reel sells when it shows one product doing one job in the first three seconds, and then tells the viewer exactly how to order it. That is the whole formula. The audio, the transitions and the text effects are decoration on top of it.


Most reseller Reels fail the same way: they open with a logo or a greeting, and the viewer has scrolled before the product appears. Instagram decides within seconds whether to push a Reel further. So does your customer.


Here is the shape that works, filmed on the phone in your hand:


- **Hook, 0–3 seconds:** the product already in use.
- **Demo, 3–15 seconds:** two or three close shots that prove it works.
- **Price and trust, 15–25 seconds:** the door price, delivery, cash on delivery.
- **One instruction, last 3 seconds:** "Message me to order."


The rest of this guide covers each piece — and how a view turns into a COD order.


## Views are not sales — decide what the Reel is for


A Reel with 50,000 views and no messages made you nothing. A Reel with 900 views and eleven messages paid for your week. Before you film, pick which one you are making, because they look different.


A reach Reel is entertainment with a product in it. A selling Reel answers a buying question: does it fit, what does it cost, how fast does it arrive, is it real. Selling Reels are quieter, shorter and less clever. They also convert.


The practical test: watch your own Reel with the sound off and ask whether a stranger could tell what the product does and what it costs. If not, it is not a selling Reel yet.


## The first three seconds decide everything


Nothing in the Reel matters if the first frame does not stop a thumb. Do not open with your face, your logo, a "hi guys", or a slow reveal. Open on the product mid-action.


Hooks that work for physical products:


- **The result first.** The stain is gone, the bag is packed, the light is on. Then rewind and show how.
- **The problem, in one shot.** A tangled drawer, a cracked phone screen, a child's toy with missing parts.
- **A hand doing the thing.** Pressing, pouring, clipping, zipping. Motion beats a still product every time.
- **A direct question on screen.** "Kitne ka?" written across the first frame works because it is the comment you get anyway.
- **The price, immediately.** For a strong deal, the number itself is the hook.


Whatever you choose, put it in the frame, not in a voiceover. Many people watch with sound off the first time.


## How to film a product Reel on a phone


You do not need a camera, a ring light or an editing suite. You need light, a steady hand and a plan for five shots.


### Light


Film next to a window in the morning or late afternoon, with the light falling on the product and your back to the window. Tube lights overhead give a flat, yellow, cheap-looking result. If you must film at night, put one lamp slightly to the side rather than straight on. Side light shows texture, and texture is what makes a product look real.


### The five shots


Film these five clips, three to five seconds each, and you have a complete Reel before you edit anything:


- **The action shot.** The product being used, filmed close.
- **The detail shot.** Stitching, buttons, fabric, finish — the thing a buyer squints at.
- **The scale shot.** The product next to a hand, a phone or a cup, so size is not a guess.
- **The full view.** The whole product, plain background, steady.
- **The packaging shot.** How it arrives at the customer's door.


Shoot vertically, fill the frame, and move the phone slowly. A shaky Reel reads as amateur even when the product is good.


### Hands in frame, no tripod needed


Hands sell. A product lying alone on a table looks like a catalogue photo; the same product held, opened or worn looks like something a person owns. You do not need to show your face if you do not want to — most top-selling reseller Reels in Pakistan are hands, product and a voice.


Prop your phone against a stack of books at a slight downward angle for overhead shots. That is the whole equipment list.


## Seven Reel formats that keep working


Rotate through these instead of inventing something new every day. Each one answers a different buying objection.


- **Unboxing.** Parcel to product in twenty seconds. Answers "will it arrive properly packed?"
- **Before and after.** Cleaning products, beauty, organisers, car accessories. The strongest format for anything with a visible result.
- **Problem to solution.** Three seconds of frustration, then the product fixing it.
- **The price reveal.** Show the product, build a guess, then put the number on screen. Works only if the price is genuinely good.
- **Three ways to use it.** One product, three uses, one Reel. Raises perceived value without a discount.
- **Packing an order.** Film a real order going out. This is trust content — it proves you actually ship.
- **Customer message screenshot.** A real delivered-and-happy message, read aloud over the product. Never fake one; a customer will notice, and that is the end of your page.


If Instagram is your main shop front, the wider setup — bio, highlights, catalogue, how to take orders without a website — is covered in[how to sell things on Instagram without a website](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/how-to-sell-things-on-instagram-without-a-website) , and[how to sell on Instagram the right way](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/how-to-sell-on-instagram-the-right-way) goes through the account basics this guide assumes you already have.


## Captions, on-screen text and hashtags


On-screen text is not the caption. On-screen text carries the sale; the caption carries the details and the search terms.


For on-screen text: three to six words per card, large, in the middle third of the screen so the interface does not cover it. Put the price on screen. A Reel that hides the price generates "price?" comments, which feels like engagement and is actually friction — half those people never come back to read your reply.


For the caption: one line that repeats the hook, one line with the specifics (size, colours, material, delivery time), one line with the instruction. Then hashtags.


On hashtags, the useful version is boring. Five to ten, mixed between product terms and city or country terms, changed to match each Reel. There is a fuller breakdown in[how to use hashtags on Instagram to promote your products](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/hashtags-for-instagram-to-promote-your-products) . Stuffing thirty generic tags does not help a selling Reel; being findable for the exact product does.


Write the caption the way you would describe the product to a customer standing in front of you. If that is where you get stuck,[how to write product descriptions that sell](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/how-to-write-product-descriptions-that-sell) has the sentence patterns, and they work just as well in a caption.


## Audio: trending sound or your own voice?


Trending audio helps distribution. Your own voice helps conversion. You want both, in the right places.


Use a trending sound for reach formats — before-and-after, three-ways-to-use-it, anything visual that does not need explaining. Use your own voiceover for anything that involves a claim, a size, a material or a price, because a human voice saying "this is real leather and it costs less than you think" is trust, and a music clip is not.


Two practical points. Keep trending audio at low volume under your voice rather than choosing one or the other. And say the important thing twice: once at the start, once at the end, since people join late.


## Turning a Reel into a cash-on-delivery order


This is the step most resellers skip, and it is the only one that pays. A view becomes an order through a path you designed, or it does not become an order at all.


- **One call to action, not three.** "Send a message to order" or "Comment PRICE" — pick one. Two instructions split the response.
- **Reply fast.** Interest in Pakistan cools within hours. A same-hour reply closes; a next-day reply gets "let me think".
- **Have a saved reply ready.** Product name, price, delivery days, cash on delivery, and the one question you need answered (size, colour, city).
- **Take the address properly.** House number, street, area, city, landmark and a working phone number. Most failed deliveries in Pakistan are an incomplete address, not a change of mind.
- **Confirm before you dispatch.** One message restating the item, the door price and the delivery day. This single habit is the difference between a profitable month and a pile of returned parcels.
- **Pin the best comment.** If someone asks the price in comments, answer publicly and pin it. Everyone else reads that reply.


Say cash on delivery out loud in the Reel. For a first-time buyer watching a page they do not know, paying at the door is the reason they risk it.


## What to film — picking products worth a Reel


Some products are simply easier to sell on video. They show a visible change, they work in ten seconds without explanation, and they solve something ordinary. Kitchen gadgets, cleaning items, organisers, beauty, phone and car accessories, kids' toys. Anything whose benefit you can prove in one shot.

## How often to post, and what to actually measure


Four to five Reels a week beats fourteen in one week and none for a month. Instagram rewards a rhythm it can predict, and so does a customer deciding whether your page is a real shop.


A workable week: three selling Reels, one trust Reel (packing an order, a customer message), one reach Reel. Film in one sitting, post through the week.


The numbers worth watching, in order:


- **Messages and comments per Reel.** The only metric attached to money.
- **Watch-through and replays.** Tells you whether the hook held. If people leave in the first three seconds, the hook is wrong, not the product.
- **Saves and shares.** A save means "I might buy this". A share means someone sold it for you.
- **Profile visits.** The step between the Reel and the order.


Likes are the one number that tells you least. Ignore them.


When a Reel works, do not just repost it — refilm it with a different hook, or post the same product in a different format. ## Mistakes that kill a selling Reel


- **Starting with a greeting.** Three seconds of "assalam-o-alaikum everyone" is three seconds of people leaving.
- **Hiding the price.** It creates comments, not orders.
- **Using the supplier's ad video as-is.** Buyers have seen it on ten pages. Your own shaky clip of the real product outsells a polished stock video, because it proves you have it.
- **Making it too long.** Under 30 seconds for a selling Reel. If the product needs two minutes to explain, it is a hard product to sell on video.
- **No instruction at the end.** People do not guess what to do next.
- **Claiming things you cannot back.** Invented delivery times, invented discounts and fake reviews all come back as refused parcels.
- **Posting and disappearing.** Reply to every comment in the first hour. Instagram watches that, and so do buyers.


## Frequently asked questions


### How long should a product Reel be?


Between 15 and 30 seconds for a selling Reel. Long enough to show the product working and say the price, short enough that most viewers reach the end. Reels that get watched fully get pushed further, so a tight 18-second Reel often travels better than a 45-second one.


### Do I need to show my face in Reels?


No. Hands and voice are enough, and plenty of Pakistani resellers sell well without ever appearing on camera. A face builds a personal brand faster, but it is not required to sell a product. What is required is that the product is clearly visible and the price is clear.


### Should I put the price in the Reel or wait for DMs?


Put it in the Reel. Withholding the price to farm comments generates a lot of replies you have to answer one by one, and most of those people never return. A visible price filters out the people who were never going to buy and brings you messages from the ones who are ready.


### What should I film if I do not have any stock yet?


Order a single unit of the product you most want to sell and film that. Because Markaz has no minimum order, that is one item rather than a carton, and you can sell the same unit afterwards. Filming the supplier's own video instead is the common shortcut, and it is why so many pages look identical.


### How many Reels should I post per week?


Four to five, consistently, is a realistic target for one person filming on a phone. Consistency matters more than volume: a page that posts five times every week for two months will out-sell one that posts twenty times in a single week and then goes quiet.


### Do Reels work for cash-on-delivery selling?


They work particularly well, because COD removes the last objection. A viewer who has never heard of your page will not enter card details, but many will agree to pay the rider at the door. Say "cash on delivery" in the Reel and put it in the on-screen text.


### Why do my Reels get views but no orders?


Usually one of three things: the Reel never showed the price, it never said how to order, or the reply came too late. Watch one of your Reels with the sound off and see whether a stranger would know what the product costs and what to do next. Then check how long your last ten replies took.
